title: ResponseEnvelope

id.description:
Created by the sender of a request. The reply carries the same ID. An
event carries a fresh ID of its own.

trace.description:
The user action this message belongs to: one ULID per action, made
by the window (or one per CLI run), carried by every request of the
action, by its replies, and by the events of the jobs and plugin
calls it started. A request without one is its own action: the core
uses its `id`. Older peers leave it out and ignore it.

oneOf.description: Reply to `ping`.

protocol_version.description: The protocol version the core speaks (`PROTOCOL_VERSION`).

oneOf.description: The request succeeded and returns no data.
The request failed.

message.description: A human-readable explanation, for logs and error dialogs.

oneOf.description: Reply to `hello`.

protocol_version.description: The protocol version the core speaks (`PROTOCOL_VERSION`).

oneOf.description: Reply to `list_directory`: the listing is complete in shared memory.

elapsed_us.description: Microseconds the core spent reading, sorting and writing it.

generation.description: 1 for the first listing, one more for every refresh.

listing_id.description: Names this listing in `close_listing` and in events.

section_handle.description:
A handle to the shared-memory section, already valid in the
client's process. The client owns it and must close it.

section_size.description:
How many bytes of the section hold the listing (the layout is in
`docs/ipc.md`).

oneOf.description: Reply to `describe_entries`: one detail per entry, from `from` on.

details.description: The entries' details, in section order.

from.description: The index of the first entry described.

generation.description:
The generation of the section the entries were read from; the
details belong to that one.

oneOf.description: Reply to `match_entries`.

generation.description: The generation of the section the names were read from.

ranges.description:
The matching indexes as `[start, count]` pairs, in order; with
`first_from`, at most one `[index, 1]`.

oneOf.description: Reply to `get_icon`.

png_base64.description: The icon as a PNG with an alpha channel, in base64.

size.description: The width and height in pixels.

oneOf.description:
Reply to `measure_paths`: every path is there, and the count has
begun.

measure_id.description:
Names the measure in `cancel_measure` and in its events; unique
for the life of the core.

oneOf.description: Reply to `volume_info`.
Reply to `list_volumes`: the volumes that answered, by drive letter.
Reply to `get_config`.

config.description:
The configuration in effect, with defaults filled in, in the
file's own format (see `sdk/config/cabinetos.schema.json`).

path.description: The configuration file the core reads.

oneOf.description: Reply to `get_value`.

value.description: The setting in effect, in the file's own format.

oneOf.description: Reply to `get_keymap`, `set_keybinding` and `reset_keybinding`.
Reply to `list_commands`.
Reply to `search_commands`: the best matches first.

hits.description: The matching commands with their scores.

oneOf.description:
Reply to `execute_command` for a command the UI runs: the core does
nothing and hands it back.
Reply to `execute_command` for a command the core ran.
Reply to `start_job`: the job exists and is queued.

job_id.description:
Names the job in later requests and events; unique for the life
of the core.

oneOf.description: Reply to `list_jobs`: every job, oldest first.
Reply to `list_plugins`: every installed plugin, by ID.

Reply to `search`: the hits, best first (names that start with the
query, then shorter names, then paths in order).

complete.description:
False when the search could not cover everything: a walk stopped
at its time or entry limit, or a volume was still being indexed.

source.description: The indexer's index, or the core's own walk.

took_us.description: How long the search took, in microseconds.

oneOf.description: Reply to `index_status`.

volumes.description: Its volumes; empty without an indexer.

oneOf.description: Reply to `terminal_open`: the shell runs.

pipe.description:
Its byte pipe: open it to read the shell's output and send it
input (one client at a time).

oneOf.description: Reply to `terminal_list`: every session, oldest first.
Reply to `list_themes`: every valid theme, by ID.
Reply to `get_theme`.

theme.description: The whole theme, as its file has it.

oneOf.description: Reply to `list_tools`: every installed Tool Extension, by ID.
Reply to `marketplace_refresh` and `marketplace_search`.

fetched_at_ms.description:
When the index was read or confirmed unchanged, in milliseconds
since 1970-01-01 UTC.

items.description:
The items, in the index's own format (camelCase keys): in index
order after a refresh, best first after a search.

source.description: Where the index came from: its URL or its file.

verified.description:
Whether the index vouches for the publisher. Shown only; publisher
identities are checked in a later version.

CapabilityInfo.description: One capability a plugin asks for.

level.description: How much it lets the plugin do.

roots.description: The folders it concerns, for `fs:read` and `fs:write`.

CapabilityLevel.description: How much a capability lets a plugin do, as the review dialog colors it.

oneOf.description: Little risk: registering commands, reading the settings.
Access to the user's files.
Reaching outside the machine or the user's secrets.

Chrome.description:
The elements of the window a theme shows or hides (`docs/themes.md`,
"Metrics and chrome"). A theme never changes a command, a key or the
layout; it may turn these on. Each one left out, like the whole object,
is as the default theme has it: off.

fkeyBar.description:
The function-key bar between the panes and the status bar: F3 View,
F4 Edit, F5 Copy, F6 Move, F7 Mkdir, F8 Delete, Alt+F1 Drive. Its
buttons run the commands those keys run.

hairlines.description:
1 px separators between the window's surfaces instead of floating
cards; with `gap` and `radiusSurface` at 0 the surfaces meet at the
hairlines.

rowStripes.description: Every other row of a file list a shade lighter.

Color.description: A colour, #RRGGBB, or #RRGGBBAA with alpha (00 clear, FF solid).

CommandInfo.description: A command, as the palette shows it.

default_keys.description: The keys it has by default.

immutable.description: Whether it belongs to the Immutable System Tier.

keys.description: The keys bound now (after the user's changes).

title.description: The human name, for example `Toggle Dual Pane`.

when.description: The context of its default bindings; absent means everywhere.

oneOf.description: Built into the core.
Registered by a plugin.

name.description: The plugin's display name, for the badge on its commands.

oneOf.description: The core runs it.
The UI runs it itself (views, panes, overlays).

DiskIdentity.description:
A physical disk. Two paths on the same `device_number` share one disk, so
copies between them compete for it.

bus_type.description:
How the disk is attached: `NVMe`, `SATA`, `USB`, `SAS`, `SCSI`, `SD`,
`RAID`, `Spaces`, `Virtual`, … or `Unknown`.

media_type.description: `HDD` or `SSD`, derived from the seek penalty; `None` when unknown.

seek_penalty.description:
Whether random access is slow (a spinning disk). `None` when the disk
does not say.

sha256.description:
The SHA-256 of the download, 64 hex digits. A download that does not
match is deleted and not installed.

url.description:
An `https:` URL, or a path relative to the index. A plugin is a zip
of `plugin.json` and `plugin.wasm`, or the `plugin.wasm` alone (its
`plugin.json` is then the item's `manifest`); a theme is its JSON
file; a tool is a zip of its folder.

EntryDetail.description: What a file pane shows beside a name, from the shell.

icon_key.description:
The icon to show, for `get_icon`: `folder` for every folder,
`ext:<extension>` (lower case, with its dot) for a file by its
extension, `generic` for a file without one, and `path:<16 hex
digits>` for an `.exe`, `.ico` or `.lnk` file, whose icon is its own.

type_name.description:
The shell's name for the type, in the user's language, for example
`Text Document` or `File folder`.

oneOf.description: The envelope was valid, but its `type` is not a request this core knows.

The frame was not a valid envelope (bad JSON, a missing or malformed
`id`, fields that do not fit the request type), or the request came
out of order, such as `list_directory` before `hello`.

The frame was longer than the 16 MiB limit. The core closes the
connection after this reply, because large data belongs in shared
memory.
The core failed while handling a valid request.
The path does not exist.
Windows denied access to the path.
The path is malformed, or it names a file where a directory is needed.
Something with that name is already there (a new folder or a rename).
No open listing on this connection has that `listing_id`.
Reading from the disk or the network failed.
No command has that ID.

The command exists but the core cannot run it yet (it arrives in a
later phase).
The keys do not follow the key grammar (`docs/keybindings.md`).

The binding would take keys another command already uses, or make a
chord's first key also a binding of its own.

The change touches the Immutable System Tier: its commands keep their
bindings, and nobody else may use their keys.

The configuration file cannot be changed now: it has an error the
user must fix first, or it cannot be written.
No job has that `job_id`.
The job has no waiting conflict with that `conflict_id`.

The resolution does not fit the conflict, such as
`delete_permanently` for a file that exists.
No plugin has that ID.

A plugin's command failed: the plugin reported an error, crashed, or
is not running.

No terminal session has that `session_id` (or its shell has exited,
for a request that needs it running).
No terminal profile has that name.

A program could not be started. A terminal's shell: its program is
not on the `PATH`, the folder does not exist, the session limit is
reached, or Windows refused. The editor of `files.editor`: its
program is neither a file nor a program on the `PATH`.
No valid theme has that ID in the themes folder.

The index has no extension with that ID (or not that version), or
none with that ID was installed from the marketplace.

The marketplace cannot do it: the index cannot be read or is refused
(plain `http:` without `marketplace.allowInsecure`), a download
failed, the download is not what its kind needs, or something is in
the way.

The download's SHA-256 is not the one the index gives. The download
was deleted and nothing was installed.
The extension needs a newer CabinetOS (`minCoreVersion`).
A Core Plugin: a WebAssembly component with its `plugin.json`.
A colour theme: one JSON file.
A Tool Extension: a folder the Tool Dock hosts.

FileHit.description: One file or directory a search found.

frn.description:
Its NTFS file reference number, when known (a 64-bit unsigned
integer; it can exceed 2^53).

FileTypeColors.description: The stroke colour of a file's icon, by its extension.

HitKind.description: Whether a hit is a file or a directory.

oneOf.description: A file (a link to a file included).
A directory (a junction or a link to a directory included).
The first index is being built; searches skip the volume.
The index is current and follows the change journal.
A new index is being built; the previous one answers meanwhile.
The volume cannot be indexed.

JobInfo.description: A job as `list_jobs` describes it: its progress and what it works on.

bytes_total.description: Bytes to copy in all; 0 for a delete or a move on one volume.

conflicts_open.description: Files waiting for a conflict decision.

current_path.description: The file being worked on now.

destination.description: The folder it copies or moves into.

elapsed_ms.description: Milliseconds since the job started working (after `queued`).

eta_seconds.description:
Seconds left at the current speed; absent in the first two seconds
and when there are no bytes to count.

files_done.description: Files and folders handled so far, skipped and failed ones included.

files_skipped.description: Of `files_done`, the ones skipped by a conflict decision.

files_total.description: Files and folders to handle in all.

items_per_second.description:
Files and folders handled per second, averaged like `speed_bps`,
with two decimals: the pace of a delete or of a move on one volume,
which move no bytes. 0 while paused and in the final record; absent
in a job's first record, before there is anything to average.

sources.description: The paths the job was started with.

speed_bps.description: Bytes per second, averaged over about the last second.

oneOf.description: Copy the sources into the destination folder.

Move the sources into the destination folder: a rename on the same
volume, a copy and then a delete of each source file across volumes.
Delete the sources.

permanent.description: Delete for good. Without it the sources go to the Recycle Bin.

JobState.description: Where a job is in its life.

oneOf.description: Waiting for its disks: another job is using them.
Walking the sources to count the files and bytes.
Working. Files waiting for a conflict decision do not change this.
Stopped by the user, or by a full disk, until resumed.
Done; every file was handled (skipped files count as handled).
Done, but some files failed.
Stopped for good by the user.
Stopped by an error that concerns the whole job.

Keymap.description:
The compiled keymap: every binding in effect. The UI runs the chord state
machine with it; the core stays the source of truth.

bindings.description: The bindings, grouped by command in registry order.

chord_window_ms.description: After the first key of a two-key chord, how long the second may take.

immutable.description:
The commands of the Immutable System Tier: their bindings cannot be
changed, and no other command may use their keys.

keys.description:
Normalized keys, for example `ctrl+shift+p` or `ctrl+k ctrl+s` (a
chord: two combinations, one after the other). Grammar in
`docs/keybindings.md`.

when.description:
The context in which the binding applies, for example `filesView`;
absent means everywhere.

MarketCapability.description: A capability a plugin asks for, as the index lists it.

level.description:
How much it lets the plugin do. The core fills it in; an index
leaves it out.

roots.description: The folders it concerns, for `fs:read` and `fs:write`.

MarketItem.description: One extension, in one version, as the index offers it.

capabilities.description:
For a plugin: the capabilities it asks for, as its `plugin.json`
lists them. The core adds each one's `level`.

description.description: One or two sentences, for the card.

download.description: Where to get it and how to check it.

id.description:
Lower case letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter: the
plugin's ID, the theme's ID or the tool's ID.

installedVersion.description:
The version installed from the marketplace, when it is installed.
The core fills it in; an index leaves it out.

installs.description: How often it was installed, when the index knows.

long.description: The long description, for the detail view.

manifest.description:
Its own manifest: the plugin's `plugin.json`, the tool's `tool.json`,
or the theme's header (`id`, `name`, `author`, `version`, `kind`,
`accent`).

minCoreVersion.description: The oldest CabinetOS it runs on, `major.minor.patch`.

rating.description: What users think of it, when the index knows.

size.description: The size of the download in bytes.

Metrics.description: The sizes a theme changes, each optional; one left out keeps the default theme's value.

backdropOpacity.description: How much the window's backdrop covers the desktop behind it: 0.86 is plain Mica, the default look; more lets less of the desktop show through behind dense text. A number from 0 to 1; left out, 0.86.

bodyPadding.description: The space between the window's edges and its surfaces, at the sides and the bottom. Whole pixels from 0 to 64; left out, 8.

captionButtonWidth.description: The width of the minimize, maximize and close buttons. Whole pixels from 24 to 96; left out, 46.

columnGap.description: The space between a file list's columns. Whole pixels from 0 to 48; left out, 0.

columnHeaderPaddingX.description: The space at each side of the column headers' row. Whole pixels from 0 to 64; left out, 14.

columnHeaderPaddingY.description: The space above and below the column headers' text. Whole pixels from 0 to 64; left out, 4.

commandBarHeight.description: The height of the command bar. Whole pixels from 14 to 80; left out, 48.

driveRowPaddingX.description: The space at each side of a drive row's content in the sidebar. Whole pixels from 0 to 64; left out, 10.

driveRowPaddingY.description: The space above and below a drive row's content in the sidebar. Whole pixels from 0 to 64; left out, 6.

editorTabHeight.description: The height of the editor's tab strip. Whole pixels from 14 to 80; left out, 36.

fieldHeight.description: The height of the address and search fields. Whole pixels from 14 to 80; left out, 32.

fkeyBarFontSize.description: The text size of the function-key bar. Whole pixels from 8 to 32; left out, 11.

fkeyBarGap.description: The space between the function-key bar's buttons. Whole pixels from 0 to 48; left out, 1.

fkeyBarHeight.description: The height of the function-key bar, when `chrome.fkeyBar` shows it (the default theme has no bar; the values left out are the handout's). Whole pixels from 14 to 80; left out, 24.

fkeyButtonRadius.description: The corner radius of a function-key button. Whole pixels from 0 to 16; left out, 2.

fontSize.description: The base text size of the window. Whole pixels from 8 to 32; left out, 13.

gap.description: The space between the window's surfaces: the sidebar, the panes and the docks. Whole pixels from 0 to 48; left out, 8.

hexColumnGap.description: The space between the hex view's columns. Whole pixels from 0 to 48; left out, 18.

hexRowHeight.description: The height of a row in the hex view. Whole pixels from 14 to 80; left out, 22.

iconButtonSize.description: The width and height of an icon button in the command bar. Whole pixels from 14 to 80; left out, 32.

lineHeight.description: The line height of the window's text, as a multiple of its size. A number from 1 to 2.5; left out, 1.4.

markdownLineHeight.description: The Markdown preview's line height, as a multiple of its text size. A number from 1 to 2.5; left out, 1.6.

markdownPaddingX.description: The space at each side of the Markdown preview's text. Whole pixels from 0 to 64; left out, 40.

markdownPaddingY.description: The space above and below the Markdown preview's text. Whole pixels from 0 to 64; left out, 28.

marketplaceCardGap.description: The space between the marketplace's cards. Whole pixels from 0 to 48; left out, 10.

marketplaceCardPaddingX.description: The space at each side of a marketplace card's content. Whole pixels from 0 to 64; left out, 14.

marketplaceCardPaddingY.description: The space above and below a marketplace card's content. Whole pixels from 0 to 64; left out, 14.

marketplaceCardRadius.description: The corner radius of a marketplace card. Whole pixels from 0 to 16; left out, 8.

marketplaceTabHeight.description: The height of a tab in the marketplace's side list. Whole pixels from 14 to 80; left out, 32.

marketplaceTabRadius.description: The corner radius of a marketplace tab. Whole pixels from 0 to 16; left out, 4.

menuRowHeight.description: The height of an item in a context menu. Whole pixels from 14 to 80; left out, 32.

modifiedColumnWeight.description: The Modified column's share, against the other weighted columns. A number from 0.1 to 10; left out, 0.55.

nameColumnMinWidth.description: The narrowest the Name column gets. Whole pixels from 0 to 400; left out, 120.

nameColumnWeight.description: The Name column's share of a file list's width, against the other weighted columns. A number from 0.1 to 10; left out, 1.

paletteRowHeight.description: The height of a row in the command palette. Whole pixels from 14 to 80; left out, 36.

paneHeaderHeight.description: The height of a pane's header, above its column headers. Whole pixels from 14 to 80; left out, 36.

radiusControl.description: The corner radius of buttons, fields and other inner controls. Whole pixels from 0 to 16; left out, 4.

radiusSurface.description: The corner radius of the panes, the sidebar, the terminal and the marketplace. Whole pixels from 0 to 16; left out, 8.

rowHeight.description: The height of a row in a file list. Whole pixels from 14 to 80; left out, 30.

rowIconGap.description: The space between a file row's icon and its name. Whole pixels from 0 to 48; left out, 10.

rowPaddingX.description: The space at each side of a file row's content. Whole pixels from 0 to 64; left out, 10.

rowRadius.description: The corner radius of a file row's selection and hover fill. Whole pixels from 0 to 16; left out, 4.

secondaryFontSize.description: The text size of a file row's Modified, Type and Size columns. Whole pixels from 8 to 32; left out, 12.

selectionBarWidth.description: The width of the accent bar at the left of a selected row, in the sidebar and in the file lists. Whole pixels from 0 to 8; left out, 3.

sidebarHeaderFontSize.description: The text size of a sidebar section's label. Whole pixels from 8 to 32; left out, 11.

sidebarHeaderPaddingBottom.description: The space below a sidebar section's label. Whole pixels from 0 to 64; left out, 4.

sidebarHeaderPaddingTop.description: The space above a sidebar section's label. Whole pixels from 0 to 64; left out, 14.

sidebarHeaderPaddingX.description: The space at each side of a sidebar section's label. Whole pixels from 0 to 64; left out, 12.

sidebarMaxWidth.description: The widest the sidebar gets. Whole pixels from 100 to 600; left out, 224.

sidebarMinWidth.description: The narrowest the sidebar gets. Whole pixels from 100 to 600; left out, 180.

sidebarRowHeight.description: The height of a workspace row and of a pinned folder's row in the sidebar; left out, a pinned folder's row keeps the default theme's 32. Whole pixels from 14 to 80; left out, 34.

sidebarRowInset.description: The space between a sidebar row and the sidebar's edges; 0 makes the rows full width. Whole pixels from 0 to 16; left out, 4.

sidebarRowRadius.description: The corner radius of a sidebar row. Whole pixels from 0 to 16; left out, 4.

sidebarWidthPercent.description: The sidebar's width as a share of the window's, kept between its narrowest and widest. Percent of the window from 5 to 50; left out, 20.

sizeColumnWidth.description: The width of the Size column. Whole pixels from 32 to 160; left out, 64.

statusBarGap.description: The space between the status bar's items. Whole pixels from 0 to 48; left out, 16.

statusBarHeight.description: The height of the status bar. Whole pixels from 14 to 80; left out, 26.

statusBarPaddingX.description: The space at each side of the status bar's content. Whole pixels from 0 to 64; left out, 14.

tabFontSize.description: The text size of a workspace tab. Whole pixels from 8 to 32; left out, 12.

tabHeight.description: The height of a workspace tab in the title bar. Whole pixels from 14 to 80; left out, 32.

tabMinWidth.description: The narrowest a workspace tab gets. Whole pixels from 40 to 240; left out, 96.

tabPaddingX.description: The space at each side of a workspace tab's text. Whole pixels from 0 to 64; left out, 14.

tabRadius.description: The radius of a workspace tab's two top corners. Whole pixels from 0 to 16; left out, 8.

tagFontSize.description: The text size of a tag chip. Whole pixels from 8 to 32; left out, 12.

tagRadius.description: The corner radius of a tag chip in the sidebar. Whole pixels from 0 to 16; left out, 12.

terminalDockHeightPercent.description: The bottom-docked terminal's height as a share of the window's, kept between its lowest and highest. Percent of the window from 10 to 80; left out, 30.

terminalDockMaxHeight.description: The highest the terminal gets when it is docked at the bottom. Whole pixels from 60 to 800; left out, 240.

terminalDockMinHeight.description: The lowest the terminal gets when it is docked at the bottom. Whole pixels from 60 to 800; left out, 120.

terminalHeaderHeight.description: The height of the terminal's header. Whole pixels from 14 to 80; left out, 34.

terminalLineHeight.description: The terminal's line height, as a multiple of its text size. A number from 1 to 2.5; left out, 1.6.

terminalPaddingX.description: The space at each side of the terminal's text. Whole pixels from 0 to 64; left out, 12.

terminalPaddingY.description: The space above and below the terminal's text. Whole pixels from 0 to 64; left out, 10.

terminalTabHeight.description: The height of a terminal session's tab. Whole pixels from 14 to 80; left out, 26.

titleBarHeight.description: The height of the title bar. Whole pixels from 14 to 80; left out, 40.

toggleHeight.description: The height of the dual and single pane toggle. Whole pixels from 14 to 80; left out, 32.

typeColumnWeight.description: The Type column's share, against the other weighted columns. A number from 0.1 to 10; left out, 0.45.

MicaTint.description: A tint laid over the Mica backdrop.

opacity.description: How much of the tint covers the backdrop: 0 (none) to 1 (all).

Palette.description:
The colours of the window. Colours with an alpha part (`#RRGGBBAA`) are
laid over the backdrop.

acrylicTint.description: The palette, context menus and flyouts (the design's acrylic).

controlFill.description: The fill of buttons and text fields.

fileTypeColors.description: The stroke of file icons, by type.

folderIcon.description: The body of the folder icon.

folderIconFront.description: The front flap of the folder icon.

layerFill.description: The fill of panes, cards and sidebar rows.

layerStrokeActive.description: The border of the focused pane.

permissionLow.description: A capability of level `low` in the review dialog.

terminalBackground.description: The terminal panel over the backdrop.

textPrimary.description: Names, titles and everything the user reads first.

textSecondary.description: Details such as dates, types and sizes.

capabilities.description: What it asks to do, for the review dialog.

commands.description: The IDs of the commands it registered (while it is active).

description.description: What it does, in a sentence or two.

id.description: The plugin's ID, from its `plugin.json`; also its folder's name.

name.description: Its display name, shown as a badge on its commands.

state.description: Where it is in its life.

PluginState.description: Where a plugin is in its life.

oneOf.description: Being compiled and started.
Running; its commands are registered.
Turned off in the configuration.

It asks for capabilities the user has not granted; it does not run
until they are.

It could not start: a bad manifest, a component that does not load,
or `activate` failed.

It trapped or ran out of time, fuel or memory; its instance was
dropped.

Rate.description: A rate per second, at least 0.

Rating.description: What users think of an extension.

count.description: How many ratings the average is of.

RequestId.description: A ULID created by the sender of a request and echoed unchanged in the reply.

SearchHit.description: One command matching a palette search.

score.description: Higher is better; only the order matters.

SearchSource.description: Where a search's hits came from.

oneOf.description: The indexer's index of whole volumes.
The core's own bounded walk of one folder tree (no indexer).

TerminalColors.description: The colours of the integrated terminal.

ansi.description:
The 16 ANSI colours: black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan,
white, then the bright ones in the same order.

background.description:
The background of the colour scheme: reverse video, and cells drawn
where the panel is opaque.

TerminalSession.description: One terminal session, as `terminal_list` reports it.

attached.description: Whether a client is attached to the byte pipe now.

cwd.description:
The folder it started in, or was last synced to. The shell may have
moved since.

pipe.description: The session's byte pipe, such as `\\.\pipe\cabinetos-term-<token>`.

profile.description: The profile it was opened with, such as `pwsh`.

session_id.description: The session's ID, unique while the core runs.

TerminalState.description: Whether a session's shell still runs.

oneOf.description: The shell runs.
The shell has exited.

code.description:
Its exit code (a Windows exit code, such as 3221225786 for a
console closed under it).

Theme.description: A colour theme: `<id>.json` in the themes folder.

$schema.description:
Where editors find the schema of the file: the core keeps
`theme.schema.json` next to the themes. The core ignores it.

accent.description: The accent colour; `null` follows the Windows accent colour.

attribution.description:
Where the colours come from and under which license, when they are
someone else's.

chrome.description:
The elements of the window this theme shows or hides. Absent: as
the default theme has them.

id.description:
Lower case letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter; also the
file's name without `.json`.

kind.description: Whether the theme is for dark mode, light mode, or follows Windows.

metrics.description:
The sizes that differ from the default theme's: a density preset
such as Commander Compact. Absent: the default theme's sizes.

mica.description: A tint over the Mica backdrop; `null` shows plain Mica.

name.description: The name people see in the theme picker.

terminal.description: The colours of the integrated terminal.

ThemeInfo.description: What the theme picker shows of a theme: `list_themes`.

accent.description: Its accent colour; `null` follows the Windows accent colour.

has_metrics.description:
Whether it sets any metric: a density preset such as Commander
Compact, which a picker may mark. `false` when an older core leaves
it out.

id.description: The theme's ID: its file's name without `.json`.

kind.description: Dark, light, or as Windows is set.

mica.description: Its tint over the Mica backdrop; `null` shows plain Mica.

ThemeKind.description: Dark, light, or as Windows is set.

oneOf.description: Light text on a dark backdrop.
Dark text on a light backdrop.

Light or dark as Windows is set; the window decides which, and
follows when the user changes it.

dir.description: Its folder, from which the Tool Dock loads it.

id.description: The tool's ID; also its folder's name.

VolumeDetails.description: The volume a path lives on, and the physical disk under it.

disk.description: The physical disk, when Windows can tell (not for network shares).

drive_letter.description: The volume's drive letter, if it has one.

free_bytes.description: Bytes free for the current user (disk quotas taken into account).

label.description: The volume label; may be empty.

volume_guid_path.description:
The volume's GUID path, for example `\\?\Volume{…}\`. Empty when the
volume has none, such as a network share.

VolumeStatus.description: One volume, as the indexer reports it.

built_in_ms.description: How long the last build took, in milliseconds.

journal_lag.description:
Change-journal bytes written but not yet applied to the index; 0 when
it is current.
